To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified 18 novel KCNB1 variants from 27 new patients with developmental and epileptic phenotypes and have expanded the mutational spectrum of KCNB.

1) we report 27 new patients with KCNB1 mutations; 2) the clinical spectrum of KCN1B‐related epilepsies is very heterogeneous; 3) the KCNB1 gene is a major gene for developmental and epileptic epilepsies.
we report the first inherited KCNB1 variant, and the first report of KCNB1‐associated epilepsy in an adult.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes that cause rare genetic diseases and how these genetic defects affect the function of cells.
the genetic and molecular basis of neurodevelopmental diseases.
the identification and characterization of genes and variants involved in developmental and epileptogenic disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

KCNB1‐associated developmental and epileptic disorders represent a new and important cause of severe neurologic disease, and that further functional and mechanistic studies of these variants will provide important insights into the underlying pathophysiology.
KCNB1‐associated epileptic encephalo‐pathies encompass a wide range of clinical presentations, with a predominant language and behavioral impairment.
KCNB1 is a gene involved in DEE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
KCNB1‐ related DEEs are a rare and heterogeneous group of disorders with variable phenotypic spectrum and prognosis, and that further research is required to better understand the pathomechanisms.
KCNB1 is a new gene in DEEs.
we have expanded the genetic and phenotypes of KCNB1 related encephalopathie.
The main takeaway from our work is that
KCNB1 variants are a rare cause of early‐onset epilepsy and DEE, and they should be systematically screened in patients with early onset of epilepsy, language and behavioral impairment.
KCNB1 is a gene involved in developmental and epileptogenic encephalopathes, which is not restricted to the epileptic phenotypes.

KCNB1 variants can be found in a large variety of developmental and epileptic phenotypes, including severe encephalopathics, and that the clinical spectrum can be expanded by the addition of new variants.
